flagged.issue: 노고치 (Dunsparce) is not built from a meaningful 노고 'effort'. The Korean name is a transliteration of the Japanese ノコッチ, which itself is an anagram-style scramble of 츠치노코 (tsuchinoko, the Japanese cryptid the Pokemon is based on). There is no 'effort' morpheme in the etymology — teaching learners that 노고 means 'effort' here invites them to misparse 노고치.

코리 in 코코리 (Phanpy) does not mean 'small'. 코코리 is built from 코끼리 (elephant) — the Pokemon is explicitly an elephant calf. The 코 of 코끼리 is doubled and clipped (코+코+리). Glossing the root as 'small' is invented; if anything the morpheme means 'elephant (clip of 코끼리)'.

Neither cited Pokemon supports 'cocoon-like body'. 콘팡 (Venonat) inherits from Japanese コンパン, where コン is from 'compound (eye)' (복안) — Venonat is a compound-eye gnat, not a cocoon. 쏘콘 (Forretress) uses 콘 from English 'cone' (Pineco/pinecone). A single gloss can't cover both, but 'cocoon-like body' fits neither.

기라스 in 마기라스 (Tyranitar), 데기라스 (Pupitar), and 애버라스 (Larvitar) is borrowed from 안기라스 — the Korean name of the kaiju Anguirus from the Godzilla franchise, which Tyranitar's line visually references. It is not a transliteration of the English suffix '-tar'. Tying the root to '-tar' obscures the kaiju reference and is etymologically wrong.

The single gloss 'sun' fits 해너츠 (Sunkern, from 해바라기 sunflower) and 해루미 (Sunflora) but is wrong for 왕눈해 (Tentacool), where 해 is a clip of 해파리 (jellyfish) — Tentacool is a jellyfish, not a sun. Lumping all three under 'sun' will mislead learners into parsing 왕눈해 as 'big-eye sun'.

샤 in 샤미드 (Vaporeon) is not an onomatopoeic 'water sound'. The widely cited Korean etymology is 샤워 (shower) + 머메이드 (mermaid). 샤 is a clip of 샤워 (English-derived 'shower'), a noun, not a water-sound mimetic. The current gloss invents an onomatopoeic reading.

잠만보 (Snorlax) plays on 잠 'sleep' + 만보, but the morphemic punchline is the colloquial 만보 ~ 만큼/매우 'a great deal' (Snorlax sleeps and eats a great deal), reinforced by Japanese カビゴン. The literal Hanja reading 萬步 'ten thousand steps' is a real Korean compound (cf. 만보계 pedometer) but is not what 잠만보 is doing — Snorlax is famously sedentary, not a stepper. 'Countless steps' is the wrong sense.

suggestion.gloss: a great deal (colloquial); also lit. 10,000 steps (萬步)

flagged.issue: The official etymology of 피죤투 (Japanese ピジョット) is 피죤 (Pigeon) + 제트 'jet' — Pidgeot is a fast-flying jet-bird, not a 'Pidgeon-2'. The 'two' reading is a folk reinterpretation widespread among Korean fans precisely because 투 looks like '2' in Korean Pokemon naming. Glossing 투 as 'two/2nd' here teaches the folk-etymology, not the actual derivation.

케인 in 브케인 (Cyndaquil) and 마그케인 (Quilava) is widely analysed as a clip of 허리케인 'hurricane' (the file even has a separate 허리케인 entry citing 마그케인). Cyndaquil/Quilava are fire-storm hedgehog Pokemon; the 'tail' reading has no support, and 'cane' (지팡이) is also unrelated. The current gloss appears made up.

골아파 is not a single morpheme or noun meaning 'headache'. 고라파덕's pun decomposes as 골(이) 아파(요) 'my head hurts' — a phrase combining the noun 골 'head' with the predicate 아프다. The standalone Korean noun for headache is 두통. Tagging 골아파 as a 'root/morpheme' meaning 'headache' is a part-of-speech and morphological error.

The cited Pokemon 왕자리 (Yanma) actually only inherits the suffix -자리, not the full noun 잠자리. The motif word 잠자리 'dragonfly' is the *source* but the realised morpheme in the name is 자리. Listing 잠자리 with componentOf: ['왕자리'] is sloppy because 잠 is dropped — learners will look in vain for 잠자리 inside 왕자리.

Direction is reversed. 이브이 is the Korean name of Eevee itself (the base species). The notes say it is 'From 에브이 (Espeon)', but 에브이 is an Eeveelution name that derives the suffix '브이' from 이브이, not the other way around. The morpheme that propagates across the eeveelutions is '브이', and 이브이 is the source word, not a sub-component of 에브이.

푸크린 (Wigglytuff) is conventionally analysed as 푸린 (Jigglypuff) + an internal infix related to 크다 'to be big' or simply a phonetic expansion to mark evolution — not a free-standing 'intensifier' morpheme that learners can productively reuse. Glossing bare 크 as 'intensifier' overstates productivity; learners taught this will try to glue 크 into other words where it doesn't go.

suggestion.gloss: from 크다 'to be big' (evolution-marker in 푸크린)

flagged.issue: The motif of 고지 (Sandslash) is pangolin (천산갑) + hedgehog, but the Korean name 고지 does not actually contain the morpheme 고슴도치. At most, the syllable 고 may be a clip, and even that is contested — many sources analyse 고지 as 고슴도치+두더지 fused, but the full morpheme 고슴도치 does not appear. componentOf: ['고지'] is misleading; the morpheme inside 고지 is just 고 at most.

suggestion.gloss: hedgehog (motif only; 고지 contains 고- at most)

flagged.issue: Gloss is too narrow. 갈다 is a high-frequency homonym whose dominant modern sense is 'to change/replace' (e.g., 칼을 갈다 'sharpen', 기름을 갈다 'change the oil', 이를 갈다 'gnash teeth'). Omitting the change/replace sense is a major omission for a freq=21 lemma.

suggestion.gloss: to change; to replace; to grind; to sharpen; to plow

flagged.issue: Gloss missing the most common modern sense, 'to drive (a vehicle)' (차를 몰다). The cattle/herding sense is correct but secondary in contemporary usage.

suggestion.gloss: to drive (a vehicle); to herd; to drive into a corner

flagged.issue: The traditional/dictionary sense of 달달 is the onomatopoeia for trembling/shivering or a rattling sound (e.g., 달달 떨다). The 'sweetly' sense is recent slang derived from 달다 'sweet' and is informal. Listing 'sweetly' first inverts the dictionary priority.

suggestion.gloss: (of trembling/shivering) shaking; (of a rattling sound); (slang) sweetly

flagged.issue: 전부 functions primarily as a noun/pronoun ('the whole; all of it') and only secondarily as an adverb ('altogether'). Tagging only as adverb misses the primary nominal usage.

Highest-frequency unglossed entry (freq 139). 부디 is a real, common adverb meaning 'please; by all means; I beg you'; the placeholder gloss should be filled in. Likely a Pokemon Center / NPC dialog filler in this corpus.

suggestion.gloss: please; by all means; I do hope (that)

flagged.issue: High-frequency placeholder gloss. 거두다 is a real verb meaning 'to harvest; to collect; to achieve (results); to withdraw'. Should be properly glossed.

suggestion.gloss: to harvest; to collect; to achieve; to withdraw

flagged.issue: Placeholder gloss. 조석 has two homonyms: 朝夕 ('morning and evening') and 潮汐 ('tides'). Could also be a fragment. Verify before glossing.

톰보이 is a Konglish loanword for 'tomboy', but very unlikely in a Pokemon ROM. Probably a Mecab over-segmentation of a katakana-derived token.

suggestion.gloss: tomboy (verify: likely Mecab artifact in this corpus)

flagged.issue: Not a standalone noun (시래기 'dried radish greens' is the lemma; 시래 alone is not a word). Likely a Mecab segmentation artifact.

아미 is a noun, not an adverb. Possible meanings: 蛾眉 'crescent eyebrow' (poetic/literary), 阿彌 'Amitabha (Buddhist)', or the BTS fandom name. None of these are adverbs. Most likely a Mecab artifact in this Pokemon corpus.

suggestion.gloss: (remove: likely Mecab artifact; literal noun senses are crescent eyebrow / Buddhist Amita)

Placeholder gloss. 윈도 is a Konglish loanword meaning 'window' (esp. computer/UI window). Unusual for a Pokemon corpus, so verify before glossing.

suggestion.gloss: window (Konglish, esp. computer window) (verify: may be Mecab artifact)

flagged.issue: Placeholder gloss. 조화 has multiple homonyms: 調和 'harmony', 造花 'artificial flower', 造化 'creation/the workings of nature'. Likely 'harmony' or 'creation' in a Pokemon context.
Placeholder gloss. 지레 as adverb = 'prematurely; in advance; ahead of time' (e.g., 지레 겁먹다 'get scared prematurely'). It is also a noun meaning 'lever' (a separate sense).

suggestion.gloss: prematurely; in advance; before its time

시티 is the Konglish loan 'city' but very unlikely in a Korean Pokemon ROM (which uses 시티 only inside compound place names and 도시 elsewhere). Probably a Mecab artifact / proper-noun fragment.

suggestion.gloss: city (Konglish) (verify: likely Mecab artifact in this corpus)

flagged.issue: The English gloss is wrong. Source is gAbilityNames[76], which in Gen 3 (LeafGreen) is the unused ability Cacophony (Japanese そうおん, lit. 'noise'). The Korean lemma 소음 ('noise') correctly corresponds to Cacophony, not Air Lock. The duplicate Air Lock entry at index 618 (에어록, gAbilityNames[77]) is the actual Air Lock; that one is correct. This entry should read 'Cacophony (ability)'. Confirmed by Bulbapedia: Cacophony is index 76 and Air Lock is index 77 in Gen 3 ability tables.

The gloss is too narrow. 몰다 broadly means 'to drive' — its primary modern senses are driving a vehicle (차를 몰다), herding animals, and driving someone into a corner (궁지에 몰다). Restricting it to 'cattle' and 'herd' suggests a rural-only word and misses the everyday vehicle sense that a TOPIK learner is likely to encounter.

suggestion.gloss: to drive (a vehicle); to herd; to drive (into)

flagged.issue: 다 in the sense 'all/entirely/everything' is an adverb (and sometimes noun), not a verb or adjective. Under the file's convention 'verb/adj' is reserved for predicate stems ending in -다; bare 다 'all' belongs in the 'noun/adv' bucket like 늘, 곧, 모두, etc.

The 'door' sense is incorrect — that is 문, not 호. 호 (號) means 'number/issue' (잡지 5월호, 101호) and is a counter for housing units; 호 (湖) means 'lake' (백두산 천지호); 호 (號) can also mean a courtesy/pen name. 'Door' looks like a confusion with the Chinese character 戶 (household), which is not a standalone Korean noun for 'door'.

suggestion.gloss: issue (number); unit (housing counter); lake; pen name

flagged.issue: Both senses listed are misleading. 'Sweet (prefix)' is not 단 standalone — it is the attributive form of 달다 (단 호박 = sweet pumpkin), a conjugation, not a lemma. 'Paragraph' is also off; the standalone noun 단 means 'platform/dais; bunch/sheaf (of vegetables); rank/level (martial arts dan); section/tier'. Paragraph in writing is typically 단락 or 문단, not bare 단.

suggestion.gloss: platform, tier; bunch, sheaf; rank (dan); section

flagged.issue: The single gloss 'department' is too narrow. 부 (部) primarily means 'part/section/division' and is a counter for copies of a book/newspaper (책 한 부); 부 (副) is the prefix 'vice-/deputy-'; 부 (富) means 'wealth/riches'. 'Department' is one specialised reading (e.g. 인사부) but is not the headword sense.

suggestion.gloss: part, section; counter for copies; (in compounds) wealth; vice-

flagged.gloss: to roll up; not to (negative imperative)
flagged.issue: The two senses listed are technically two different (homophonous) verbs. 말다₁ = to roll up (김밥을 말다, 소매를 말다); 말다₂ = the auxiliary verb used in -지 말다 negative imperatives. Combining them in one entry is dictionary-acceptable but the gloss obscures that the negative-imperative use almost never appears as a standalone verb — it is grammaticalised.

suggestion.gloss: to roll up; (auxiliary, in -지 말다) don't, stop

flagged.issue: 'To be hateful' implies the subject is the one feeling hatred, which is the opposite of 밉다's meaning. 밉다 is a descriptive verb meaning the subject is the object of dislike — 'to be disliked, to look unpleasant, to be ugly/loathsome'. A more accurate gloss is 'to be despicable, to be hated/disliked' or 'to be ugly (in behaviour or looks)'.

suggestion.gloss: to be detestable, dislikable; (of a person/behaviour) ugly

flagged.issue: 바다 is unambiguously a noun meaning 'sea'. The partOfSpeech tag 'verb/adj' is wrong; it should be 'noun/adv' to match the convention used for the other noun entries in the file. The gloss itself is correct.

술잔 specifically denotes a vessel for alcohol (술 = alcohol + 잔 = cup), e.g. wineglass, shot glass, sake cup. The gloss 'drinking cup' is too generic and could be misread as a water cup. A more precise gloss would specify alcohol.

짓 in modern Korean almost always carries a negative or pejorative connotation (e.g. 미친 짓, 나쁜 짓, 바보 같은 짓). The neutral gloss 'act, gesture' loses this nuance and a learner could mistakenly apply it to neutral actions where 행동 would be correct.

고기 in modern Korean primarily means 'meat'. The 'fish' sense survives only in compounds like 물고기 (live fish) and as an archaic/historical reading; standalone 고기 for fish-as-food is uncommon and 생선/물고기 are used instead. Listing 'fish' as a coequal gloss may mislead learners.

suggestion.gloss: meat (also archaic/compound: fish, as in 물고기)

flagged.issue: 식 standalone does not mean 'meal'. The 'meal' sense only appears in compounds like 식사, 한식, 양식. Bare 식 means 'ceremony', 'formula' (math), or 'expression/style'. Listing 'meal' as a standalone gloss is misleading for learners.

Standalone 한 is the native-Korean numeral determiner 'one' (한 사람 = one person), or a prefix/intensifier ('한가운데' = the very middle). It does not mean 'Korean' on its own; the 'Korean' sense only emerges in Sino-Korean compounds like 한국, 한복, 한식. PoS should be 'determiner' rather than 'noun/adv'.

suggestion.gloss: one (native numeral, prenominal); the very (intensifier prefix)

flagged.issue: 맨 is primarily a prefix meaning 'bare/naked, nothing but' (맨손 'bare hand', 맨발 'bare foot', 맨바닥 'bare ground'). Only as a determiner before nouns of position/order does it intensify to 'the very (most)' (맨 앞, 맨 처음). The current gloss captures only the secondary sense and omits the dominant 'bare' meaning.

suggestion.gloss: bare, naked (prefix); the very (most), foremost (before position/order nouns)

flagged.issue: The gloss correctly identifies 여 as a prefix (Sino-Korean 女, used in 여학생, 여배우, 여왕). However the partOfSpeech 'noun/adv' contradicts the gloss; it should be 'prefix'. 여 does not function as a standalone noun or adverb.

기본 is a noun meaning 'foundation, basis, fundamentals' (Sino-Korean 基本). 'basic' is an adjective in English, but 기본 itself is a noun (the adjective form is 기본적 or 기본의/기본적인). Glossing as 'basic' invites the learner to use 기본 as an adjective, which is wrong.

중요 is recognized in dictionaries as a noun meaning 'importance', but in actual usage it is overwhelmingly bound: 중요하다 (adj), 중요한 (modifier), 중요성 (the noun 'importance'). Standalone 중요 is rare, and learners may produce ungrammatical sentences. The headword would be more useful as 중요하다.

적 has multiple unrelated homographs: 적 (敵) 'enemy', 적 (跡/迹) 'time/moment, occasion' (used in 어렸을 적에), and the productive Sino-Korean suffix 적 (的) 'pertaining to' (사회적, 과학적). The gloss 'time when' is awkward English for the temporal sense; the suffix 적(的) sense is also missing. The two listed senses are unrelated lexemes.

suggestion.gloss: enemy (敵); occasion, time (어렸을 적에); -ic, -al (suffix 的)

flagged.issue: Both senses are real (plural particle -들 and noun 들 'field/plain'), but they are different parts of speech: the plural marker is a particle/suffix, while 들 'field' is a noun. PoS 'noun/adv' covers neither cleanly. 들 is also never an adverb.

Both senses are correct, but 장 is one of the most polysemous Sino-Korean syllables (chapter 章, market 場, sheet-counter 張, intestines 腸, head/chief 長, sauce 醬, etc.). For a learner-facing seed, listing only two arbitrary senses out of many is misleading. Also, 장 as a counter is not an adverb.

suggestion.gloss: sheet, page (counter for flat objects); chapter (章); market (場)

flagged.issue: Both senses exist (drum 북, north 北), but bare 북 for 'north' is mostly bound — natural usage is 북쪽 or 북부. 북 as 'drum' is a pure-Korean noun and is fully standalone. Listing 'north' first as a coequal gloss may lead learners to produce *'북에 있다' instead of '북쪽에 있다'.

suggestion.gloss: drum (instrument); north (mostly in compounds: 북쪽, 북부)

flagged.issue: 이렇다 is the dictionary form of an adjective meaning 'to be like this, to be such'. The gloss 'like this' reads as the adverbial form 이렇게 ('in this way'). For the headword 이렇다, a more accurate gloss would be 'to be like this; to be this way'.

suggestion.gloss: to be like this, to be such

flagged.issue: 이리 in modern Korean is an adverb ('this way, hither, like this'), not a noun. The 'noun' option in 'noun/adv' is wrong. (Historically 이리 also meant 'wolf' but that sense is now obsolete in favor of 늑대.)
딱 is an adverb meaning 'exactly, precisely, just right' (딱 맞다, 딱 한 번). It is also a mimetic for snapping/cracking sounds. It is not a noun. The 'noun' element of 'noun/adv' is wrong.

제법 in this sense ('quite, considerably, fairly') is an adverb (제법 잘하다, 제법 춥다). The homograph noun 제법 (製法) 'method of manufacture' is unrelated and not the gloss given. PoS 'noun/adv' is misleading for the gloss 'quite, fairly'.
주로 is unambiguously an adverb meaning 'mainly, mostly, primarily'. PoS should be 'adverb', not 'noun/adv'. The homograph 주로 (走路) 'racetrack' is a different lexeme not represented by this gloss.
전혀 is an adverb ('not at all, never', requires negative predicate). PoS 'noun/adv' is incorrect — it is never used as a noun.

suggestion.gloss: not at all, (not) in the least

flagged.issue: 온통 is an adverb ('all over, entirely, throughout', as in 온통 빨갛다). PoS should be 'adverb'.
이미 is unambiguously an adverb ('already'). It is never used as a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.
대단히 (the -히 form) is unambiguously an adverb ('very, extremely, greatly'). It is never a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.
완전히 (the -히 form) is unambiguously an adverb. PoS should be 'adverb'. (The noun is 완전.)
함께 is unambiguously an adverb. PoS should be 'adverb'.
오랫동안 functions adverbially ('for a long time'). It is morphologically a noun phrase (오랜 + 동안) but is not used as a standalone noun in modern usage; it occupies an adverbial slot.

정말 is most often used as an adverb ('really'), though it is also a noun ('the truth, real fact'). Tagging 'noun/adv' is technically defensible but for the gloss 'really' specifically, it should be 'adverb'.

suggestion.gloss: really, truly (adv); the truth, real fact (noun)

flagged.issue: 지금 functions as both a noun ('the present (moment)') and an adverb ('now'); the dual tag is reasonable. Including for completeness — no flag needed unless tag granularity matters elsewhere.
게다가 is a conjunctive adverb ('moreover, in addition, on top of that'). It is never a noun. PoS should be 'adverb' or 'conjunction'.

suggestion.gloss: moreover, in addition, on top of that

flagged.issue: 그대로 is an adverb ('as it is, just like that, intact'). It can also occupy noun-phrase slots loosely, but is not classified as a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.

suggestion.gloss: as it is, just like that, intact

flagged.issue: 가만히 (-히 form) is an adverb ('quietly, still, motionlessly'). It is never a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.
없이 is an adverb ('without'), derived from 없다 + -이. It is never a noun.
아 is an interjection (exclamation). PoS should be 'interjection', not 'noun/adv'. (As a vocative particle 아 is a particle, also not a noun/adv.)

그만 is primarily an adverb ('that much; stop it; involuntarily/unintentionally'). The gloss 'stop' is misleading because 그만 is not the imperative verb 'stop'; it is the adverbial '(do) no more, enough'. A learner could mistakenly use it as a verb.

거 is the colloquial contracted form of the bound noun 것 ('thing, fact'). It is bound — it cannot stand alone as a free noun. Listing it as 'noun/adv' without indicating its bound status may mislead learners into producing ungrammatical *거가 instead of 게/것이.

suggestion.gloss: thing, fact (bound noun, colloquial form of 것)

flagged.issue: 년 is a bound counter for years (2024년, 삼 년) — it cannot stand as a free noun meaning 'year' (the free noun is 해). Tagging as 'noun/adv' obscures its counter status.
인분 is a counter (Sino-Korean 人分) for food portions (이 인분 = two servings). PoS 'noun/adv' is incorrect; it should be 'counter'. The gloss already correctly identifies it as a counter.

고프다 is a bound adjective that essentially only collocates with 배 (배(가) 고프다 = 'to be hungry', literally 'stomach is empty/hungry'). It cannot freely mean 'hungry' attached to a person; *나는 고파요 is awkward. Without the 배 collocation note, learners produce ungrammatical sentences.

suggestion.gloss: (of stomach) to be hungry; used as 배가 고프다

flagged.issue: 피시 is the Hangulization of 'PC'. While it appears in Korean (especially 피시방 'PC bang'/internet cafe), in everyday writing the Roman letters 'PC' are far more common. As a TOPIK 1+2 headword, 피시방 (PC room) would be more useful than the bare transliteration.

똑같이 is an adverb meaning 'identically / in the same way / equally', describing how an action is done. The English gloss 'exactly the same' reads as an adjectival phrase modifying a noun. A learner seeing this gloss could mis-use it as an adjective. Better gloss: 'identically; in the same way; equally'.

전자 is a noun with two main senses: 電子 'electron' (the physics particle) and 前者 'the former' (in comparisons, opposite of 후자 'the latter'). The current gloss 'electronic' is an English adjective and only loosely covers usage in compounds like 전자제품. Standalone 전자 is not adjectival. Better: 'electron; the former'.

연기 has three common homonyms: 煙氣 'smoke', 演技 'acting/performance', and 延期 'postponement'. The third sense (postponement) is arguably the most frequent in everyday written Korean (회의를 연기하다). Listing only two senses is not strictly wrong but is incomplete. Consider adding 'postponement'.
